assertions.text: Tests use @Test(arguments:) parameterised cases — not one test function per case, and not a loop over cases inside a single test body.
Test function bodies contain no for/while loops or forEach — cases are supplied via @Test(arguments:), not iterated manually.
Test function bodies contain no if/switch/guard branching — expected outcomes come from the argument rows, not branching logic.
assertions.evidence: No if/switch/guard statements in @Test function bodies

assertions.text: Each case reads as a coherent row pairing input with expected outcome — labelled tuple elements, a row struct, or zip of collections — not multiple independent collections passed to arguments
assertions.evidence: struct CancellationFeeCase { let scenario: String; let bookingValue: Int; let daysBeforeCheckIn: Int; let expectedFee: Int }

assertions.text: Every fee tier is represented (free, 50%, 80%, full value) and every boundary is tested from both sides: 30 days (free) vs 29 days (50%), 7 days (50%) vs 6 days (80%), 1 day (80%) vs 0 days (full value)
assertions.evidence: daysBeforeCheckIn: 30 expectedFee: 0; 29 expectedFee: 100; 7 expectedFee: 100; 6 expectedFee: 160; 1 expectedFee: 160; 0 expectedFee: 200

assertions.text: The started-stay case is expressed as its own test using #expect(throws:) — not mixed into the fee table via sentinel values, optional expectations, or branching inside the test body
assertions.evidence: @Test("Cancelling once the stay has started...") func cancellationAfterStayStarted... #expect(throws: CancellationError.stayAlreadyStarted)

assertions.text: Case values are concrete domain values (days like 29, fees like 100 for a 200-euro booking) — not abstract placeholders, computed expressions like bookingValue / 2, or symbolic constants that hide the actual numbers from the reader
assertions.evidence: CancellationFeeCase(scenario: "mid-way through the half-price window", bookingValue: 340, daysBeforeCheckIn: 15, expectedFee: 170) and CancellationFeeCase(scenario: "mid-way through the eighty-percent window", bookingValue: 150, daysBeforeCheckIn: 3, expectedFee: 120)

assertions.text: swift build --build-tests succeeds against the package scaffolding
